Claim: app/pages/ the material pages' renderer, run by the build in Node. Imports ui/ and engine/; nothing imports it
Finding: Not literally true, and the one outward import is missing. The build loads it (stage 8), the tools and the page check import it, and stage.js itself imports the build's cache module, so "imports ui/ and engine/" is not all it imports.
Evidence: build/src/index.js:122 `await import('../../app/pages/stage.js')`; app/pages/stage.js:24 `import { ... } from '../../build/src/build-cache.js'`; scripts/pages/render.mjs and test/pages.check.js import app/pages/render.js. Nothing under app/js imports app/pages (grep).
Fix: Imports ui/ and engine/ (stage.js also the build's cache, build/src/build-cache.js). Nothing in app/ imports it; the build's stage 8 loads it.

Claim: (the facts, words, numbers and scale above) and decide nothing
Finding: "numbers" is not among the ui/ modules listed above. numbers.js is a module of app/pages (listed in the table below, with findings.js and html.js); the ui/ modules the pages read are facts, words, stats and scales.

Evidence: app/pages/stage.js:134 `index (${mb} MB)` with mb = total of every file; dist/manifest.json pages.bytes = 30628168 (29.2 MB); site/materials/index.html is 101,081 bytes.
Fix: Say the figure is the set's: "index (the set, 29.2 MB)" in the doc, or change the printed line to "set (29.2 MB)". Keep the example current.

Claim: `npm run pages -- M020 M001` (or `--all`): renders material pages into `dist/materials/` while their design is worked on
Finding: Would mislead a maintainer: the tool first empties dist/materials/ and, when given ids, writes only those materials (plus index and assets). The folder then no longer matches dist/manifest.json, so `pages:check` (P1, P14) fails until `npm run build`, and with the selector file absent the page links differ from the build's.
Evidence: scripts/pages/render.mjs:55 `rmSync(out, { recursive: true, force: true })`; :47 `if (!all) env.only = ids`; app/pages/render.js:169 `.filter((id) => !env.only || env.only.includes(id))`; scripts/pages/render.mjs:46 selectorFile is null when the selector is not in dist/.
Fix: renders material pages into dist/materials/ for design work, after emptying it: only the named materials (or all with --all); run `npm run build` before `pages:check`.

Claim: | typical (of a material), headline | median of its products, key property |
Finding: The pages do not follow this row for "typical": every material page uses "typical" as a defined term (a "Typical" column, "Typical values, and where each sits among the materials", "typically 6 kJ/m²"), and INTERFACE itself says "typical numbers" at line 655. P9 does not enforce this row (its COINAGES list has no "typical"), so the Words table and the pages disagree and no check says which wins.
Evidence: Built page M020: "### Typical values, and where each sits among the materials"; table column "Typical"; "Typical is the median of the products compared"; "Notched Charpy impact is typically 6 kJ/m²". test/pages.check.js:936 COINAGES has no "typical".
Fix: Either add a note to the row ("on the material pages 'typical' is used and defined once as the median of the products compared") or reword the pages. Do not leave the table saying the page says "median of its products" only.

Claim: shaped by filler as every view shapes it (D110: circle unfilled, diamond carbon fibre, square glass fibre, triangle ESD, star foaming, hexagon an undisclosed variant)
Finding: True but would mislead since the 2026-10-17 wording pass. The "undisclosed" reinforcement facet also holds materials whose filler is named (aramid fibre, ceramic, PTFE, glass spheres, graphene, natural fibre, metal powder, conductive filler). The material page and the drawer's lede now name that filler; the rail and chart labels still say "Other variant, filler not disclosed", so one material is described two ways and the doc does not say the hexagon covers named fillers.
Evidence: app/js/ui/labels.js:73 FILLER.undisclosed = 'Other variant, filler not disclosed' (still used by app/js/ui/filters.js:202); labels.js:76-91 namedFiller and its comment "files it with the undisclosed variants"; built page M106 masthead: "Filler: Aramid fibre", "A variant with aramid fibre."
Fix: hexagon a variant whose filler is not the unfilled base polymer's (undisclosed, or named by the materials table as aramid fibre, ceramic, PTFE and the like); say that the chart and rail label stays "Other variant, filler not disclosed" for these.

Claim: what is **not drawn**, by setting and why (a chamber that needs none, an enclosure asked for with no temperature, a window that gives only one end, a drying statement with no temperature)

Fix: by setting and why (nothing in any sheet, shared sheet or guide row: "say nothing"; a chamber that needs none; an enclosure asked for or recommended with no temperature; room temperature; a window that gives only one end; a drying statement with no temperature)

Claim: a GitHub release `h2c-<release>` with the selector's page, its manifest and `H2C_Material_Pages_<snapshot>_<release>.zip`, the material pages zipped ... A release kept before it had its zip gets it on the next build of that release.
Finding: True but would mislead: the zip is made once per release ID and then kept. A change to the pages' design alone is not a new release (D96, D142), so the zip of an existing release keeps the first design it was built with while the site serves the newer pages; the sentence reads as if the zip tracks the site.
Evidence: .github/workflows/pages.yml:76-79 and :89-93 ("one that has a zip keeps it"); build/src/release.js RELEASE_INPUTS has no app/pages; docs/INTERFACE.md:690-691.
Fix: add: "The zip is written once for a release and kept; a later change to the pages' design alone changes the site's pages, not that release's zip."

Claim: Editorial, Record tier: it decides nothing (D142)
Finding: Wrong tier. The record tier (D85) is what a source prints that no row holds, derived into dist/h2c.sqlite, stored nowhere under data/tables, read by neither the build nor the page. material_summaries.csv is a stored table, read by the build into db.json (materials[].written) and shown on the pages.
Evidence: DECISIONS.md:2331 and :2341 (D85: "Nothing is stored under `data/tables`", "The build does not read it, the page does not ship it"); build/src/compile.js:710 attachWritten; scripts/data/sqlite.mjs:349 the table is tier 'raw'.
Fix: Editorial: it decides nothing (D142).

Claim: one row per material with a page
Finding: True of the tool that adds rows and of the page check, not of the build. The build refuses a row only for a family entry or an unknown material; a row for a material that has no page (or one that lost it when products were retired or measurements held back) builds, and is caught only by pages:check P12 in verify.
Evidence: build/src/written.js:181 (only `!m || m.familyEntry` is refused); scripts/pages/add-summaries.mjs:58 refuses no-page at add time; test/pages.check.js:1000 P12 "a written summary on a material with no page".
Fix: one row per material with a page (the build refuses a row on a family entry; pages:add-summaries and pages:check refuse one on a material below the page rule)

Claim: `build:diff` shows 0 differences and templates.csv is unchanged.

Also build:diff builds without the pages (--no-pages), so it says nothing about them.

Claim: Moving the drawer onto that layer changed none of its 11,900 renders by a byte. Where a page needs a number the build does not hold, it is compiled, never worked out in the page alone
Finding: Two statements read as standing rules and are not. (1) The drawer's renders have since changed on purpose through the shared words: step 5 moved the Printing tab's "Not drawn" line (530 of 11,900 renders, 106 materials) and the Overview lede of 18 materials (270 renders); D142 does not record it. (2) Pages do work out numbers the build does not hold: print-window counts and medians, ranks, layer shares and map positions are computed at render time in material-stats.js, material-facts.js and print-spread.js (stated in the next clause as display statistics, but "never in the page alone" is not what the code does).
Evidence: git show fc1efeb5 (message: "530 of the 11,900 golden renders", "270 renders"); app/js/ui/material-stats.js printWindows/compareMedians/layerPairs; app/js/ui/print-spread.js; ARCHITECTURE.md:263 "worked out on the page and deciding nothing".
Fix: Add to D142: "step 5 (2026-10-17) changed the shared words, so the drawer's Printing 'Not drawn' line and the Overview lede moved on purpose"; and reword (2) to "a number the build does not hold is a display statistic in material-stats.js, worked out at render time and deciding nothing".

Claim: npm run build:diff    # what the change did to the compiled database, against HEAD
Finding: Would mislead a maintainer following the list in order: build:diff builds the working tree with --no-pages, which removes dist/materials/ and rewrites dist/db.json and the manifest without pages. Afterwards `npm run pages:check` and `pages:text` stop with "run npm run build".
Evidence: scripts/build-diff.mjs:28-30 (`index.js --no-pages`); build/src/index.js:121-123 `rmSync(dist/materials)`; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:719-720 says it only in passing.
Fix: add: "(it builds without the material pages and removes dist/materials/; run npm run build before pages:check or pages:text)".

Claim: It types no number: at most two, each a placeholder the build fills ... a paragraph of 60 to 100 words
Finding: Read as rules, but nothing checks them: pages:add-summaries only prints a note for a summary outside 60 to 100 words ("said, not refused") and nothing counts numbers; SUMMARY-NUMBER finds only a number typed by hand. (The 76 rows do all keep to it: 61-100 words, at most two number placeholders.) Also `pages:fields` and `pages:text` run a full `npm run build` first when dist/db.json is older than data/, schema/ or build/src, although their headers say they write nothing.
Evidence: scripts/pages/add-summaries.mjs:12-13 comment and :68 `notes.push(...)`; scripts/pages/lib.mjs:19-24 loadDb spawns `npm run build`; scripts/pages/fields.mjs:10 "writes nothing".
Fix: say "the checklist asks for 60 to 100 words and at most two numbers; the tool notes the words and checks neither the count of numbers nor the length", and note that fields/text build first where dist/db.json is stale.

Claim: it refuses the whole file for a material with no page, a placeholder the build cannot fill (SUMMARY-PLACEHOLDER) or a number typed by hand (SUMMARY-NUMBER)
Finding: True of pages:add-summaries; the build does not give a material with no page the same refusal. A material that falls below the page rule later (products retired, values held back) keeps its row, the build passes, and the failure comes only from pages:check P12 in verify. AGENTS.md:300 says a data change stops the build with SUMMARY-PLACEHOLDER only for an unfillable placeholder.
Evidence: build/src/written.js:181; test/pages.check.js:1000.
Fix: add: "A data change that takes a material below the page rule leaves its row, and pages:check (P12) then fails: retire the row with the page, never leave it."

Claim: `verify` runs it after the snapshot check (scripts/verify.mjs)
Finding: Stale step order. Since D144 the step follows only the build and runs beside the snapshot, the audit and the other data steps.
Evidence: scripts/verify.mjs:58-60 `['material pages', 'npm', ['run', 'pages:check'], afterBuild]`; scripts/verify.mjs header (D144).
